parts/shell.mjs is unchanged: it made 22,734 blocks with 0 refused writes and no off-palette blocks of its own. The 8 OFF-PALETTE entries come from the roof, not the shell: runParts lays roof.json right after the shell, and roof-texture.mjs's "slate" material mix emits tuff_bricks, stone_brick, cobbled/polished_deepslate stairs and slabs. Those are not in palette.json.
The shell line in make.sh shows neither REFUSED nor OFF-PALETTE, but parts-report.json still lists the 8 roof entries under "mansion shell". Build.nbt is written, so the build is whole.
Fixing them means changing roof.json's material, or the slate texture, or palette.json, and none of those is parts/shell.mjs, so I stopped.

waste.what: Working out which module emitted the OFF-PALETTE blocks: grepping the minecraft-design tools for tuff_brick and cobbled_deepslate, then reading the slate mix in roof-texture.mjs
waste.cost: about 4 greps and 2 reads, roughly 10K tokens
waste.tool: runParts report should tag each block by the stage that wrote it, with the roof as its own 'roof' stage and not part of the shell. Or `mcd roof --dry-run roof.json --palette palette.json` should name the material source for each off-palette block, e.g. 'slate mix eave tuff_brick (roof-texture.mjs)'

waste.what: Confirming the shell's own writes are clean by reading parts-report.json and checking the make.sh lines against it
waste.cost: 1 report read plus 2 make.sh runs, about 20 seconds of build time
waste.tool: make.sh's per-part line should split roof blocks out (for example 'roof: 8 off-palette, not this part'). Then a shell-only OFF-PALETTE report would not wrongly blame the part

companions.task: Pick the slate-look roof blocks that are in palette.json (deepslate_tiles, deepslate_tile_stairs and slabs, polished_deepslate, cobbled_deepslate) to replace the tuff and stone_brick eave/ridge, and say whether the stairs and slabs of cobbled and polished deepslate should be added to palette.json.
Check the civic roof's eave, ridge and fascia so the roof.json material swap keeps the same look: the cornice reads as stone-grey, and the cobbled/polished mix stays at the same proportions.

left: OFF-PALETTE (roof-owned, not shell): tuff_brick_slab x258, tuff_bricks x176, cobbled_deepslate_stairs x259, tuff_brick_stairs x228, cobbled_deepslate_slab x285, polished_deepslate_slab x114, polished_deepslate_stairs x122, stone_brick_slab x46. They come from roof.json material "slate" via roof-texture.mjs (eave tuff_brick, ridge stone_brick, mix cobbled/polished deepslate). Fix in roof.json (material) or roof-texture.mjs, or by adding these variants to palette.json. Those files are not mine, so I did not touch them.
The shell still shows these 8 entries under "mansion shell" in parts-report.json, because runParts attributes the roof's writes to the part before it. make.sh's per-part line for the shell is clean.

Room parts (entrance hall, parlour, dining, butler's pantry, powder room, kitchen, bedroom 3, bedroom 5, bedroom 6, ground gallery, cottage bath, gazebo, greenhouse) REFUSE writes into cells the shell left as air, such as the shell's carved rooms. That is not the shell's problem, so I did not change the shell for it. But it does show the shell has no furniture-ready floors in those spots. Each room owner should be told.

parts/shell.mjs is unchanged: it made 22,734 blocks with 0 refused writes and no off-palette blocks of its own. The 8 OFF-PALETTE entries come from the roof, not the shell: runParts lays roof.json right after the shell, and roof-texture.mjs's "slate" material mix emits tuff_bricks, stone_brick, cobbled/polished_deepslate stairs and slabs. Those are not in palette.json.
The shell line in make.sh shows neither REFUSED nor OFF-PALETTE, but parts-report.json still lists the 8 roof entries under "mansion shell". Build.nbt is written, so the build is whole.
Fixing them means changing roof.json's material, or the slate texture, or palette.json, and none of those is parts/shell.mjs, so I stopped.

waste.what: Working out which module emitted the OFF-PALETTE blocks: grepping the minecraft-design tools for tuff_brick and cobbled_deepslate, then reading the slate mix in roof-texture.mjs
waste.cost: about 4 greps and 2 reads, roughly 10K tokens
waste.tool: runParts report should tag each block by the stage that wrote it, with the roof as its own 'roof' stage and not part of the shell. Or `mcd roof --dry-run roof.json --palette palette.json` should name the material source for each off-palette block, e.g. 'slate mix eave tuff_brick (roof-texture.mjs)'

waste.what: Confirming the shell's own writes are clean by reading parts-report.json and checking the make.sh lines against it
waste.cost: 1 report read plus 2 make.sh runs, about 20 seconds of build time
waste.tool: make.sh's per-part line should split roof blocks out (for example 'roof: 8 off-palette, not this part'). Then a shell-only OFF-PALETTE report would not wrongly blame the part

companions.task: Pick the slate-look roof blocks that are in palette.json (deepslate_tiles, deepslate_tile_stairs and slabs, polished_deepslate, cobbled_deepslate) to replace the tuff and stone_brick eave/ridge, and say whether the stairs and slabs of cobbled and polished deepslate should be added to palette.json.
Check the civic roof's eave, ridge and fascia so the roof.json material swap keeps the same look: the cornice reads as stone-grey, and the cobbled/polished mix stays at the same proportions.

left: OFF-PALETTE (roof-owned, not shell): tuff_brick_slab x258, tuff_bricks x176, cobbled_deepslate_stairs x259, tuff_brick_stairs x228, cobbled_deepslate_slab x285, polished_deepslate_slab x114, polished_deepslate_stairs x122, stone_brick_slab x46. They come from roof.json material "slate" via roof-texture.mjs (eave tuff_brick, ridge stone_brick, mix cobbled/polished deepslate). Fix in roof.json (material) or roof-texture.mjs, or by adding these variants to palette.json. Those files are not mine, so I did not touch them.
The shell still shows these 8 entries under "mansion shell" in parts-report.json, because runParts attributes the roof's writes to the part before it. make.sh's per-part line for the shell is clean.

Room parts (entrance hall, parlour, dining, butler's pantry, powder room, kitchen, bedroom 3, bedroom 5, bedroom 6, ground gallery, cottage bath, gazebo, greenhouse) REFUSE writes into cells the shell left as air, such as the shell's carved rooms. That is not the shell's problem, so I did not change the shell for it. But it does show the shell has no furniture-ready floors in those spots. Each room owner should be told.
